Resp  Through: Mr. Satish Kumar, APP for the St  with SI Hawa Singh, P.S. Mango  Mr. Sumesh Gandhi, Mr. Manoj a  Mr. Bankebihari, Advocates for  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE SWARANA KANTA SHARMA  ORDER % 20.02.2023 CRL.M.A. 4539/2023 (exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C.) has been filed on behalf of petitioners seeking quashing of FIR no. 735/2019 registered at Police Station Mangolpuri, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (IPC).
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Satish Kumar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. B.K.
Pandey and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Hawa Singh, Police Station Mangolpuri, Delhi.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 22.06.2018.
No child was born from the said wedlock.
It is stated that due to temperamental differences, parties started living separately since 01.09.2018.
On the complaint of respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no. 735/2019 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC was registered at Police Station Mangolpuri, Delhi against petitioners.

During the pendency of the present FIR, parties had amicably settled their disputes and entered into a Sh. Prashant Sishodia. & Ors vs State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) & Anr on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61044270/

7.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled/compromised between them and they have obtained decree of divorce by mutual consent from the concerned Court.
8. Respondent no. 2 further states that she has not been able to sign the petition since she was not informed at the time of filing of the petition.
She, however, states that she has entered into the Settlement Agreement dated 31.01.2022 voluntarily, which is already on record as Annexure P-3.
Considering that the respondent no. 2 has made her statement before this Court in person and that the Settlement Agreement signed by respondent no. 2 is on record, the present FIR be quashed.

9. It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family member.

10. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 2,00,000/- in three installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 40,000/- paid to respondent no.2 at the time of recording statements in the first motion petition.
b. Second installment of Rs. 40,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording statements in the second motion petition.

c.
Third/Final instalment of Rs. 1,20,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.

11. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 1,20,000/- today, i.e., 20.02.2023 vide Cheque No.250094 dated 17.02.2023 drawn on Bank of Baroda, New Delhi and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

12. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings

,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

13. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 735/2019 registered at Police Station Mangolpuri, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
14. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of.
